we provide a unified approach to likelihood inference on stochastic ordering for a wide class of models, including the classical models of stochastic orderings in a nonparametric context.

, in a non-parametric context, the problem of stochastic orderings can be solved by a general estimation algorithm and the corresponding log-likelihood ratio test has a simple asymptotic distribution.

we have unified the theory of stochastic ordering in the nonparametric context and have shown that the maximum likelihood estimator of a stochastic ordering is a linear transformation of the maximum likelihood estimator under the null hypothesis of identical distributions, and that the asymptotic distribution is a linear transformation as well.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the stochastic orderings considered here can be treated as a special case of a more general class of hypotheses, which can be formulated as a set of linear inequalities on a vector of conditional distributions.

, for data in a two way contingency table with ordered rows and columns, stochastic orders are equivalent to requiring that a vector of conditional probabilities satisfies an appropriate system of linear inequalities.
the likelihood ratio test for stochastic ordering is asymptotically equivalent to a test for the corresponding linear inequality.
